scope: Proposition 13.1 (Two compact periodic processors) of the manuscript “Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows” (preprints/Prefix-Instructions-and-Incompressible-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8cd581420ec9967a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every deterministic machine and finite input, and every fixed computable viscosity ν > 0, there are effective smooth velocities U and forces f on R3 with the following properties. Both have all mixed derivatives bounded, support in a compact spatial set independent of time, and period one for t ≥ 1; U(0) = 0. The solution with pressure zero is unique in the class u ∈ C([0, T]; H2 ) ∩ C1 ([0, T]; L2 ), p ∈ C([0, T]; H1 ), sup [0,T]×R3 (|u| + |∇u|) < ∞ for every finite T, and its kinetic energy is uniformly bounded. The following are two separate constructions with their stated fixed particle events: 1. Four successive stationary localized fields, with initial label (−1, 0, 0) and detector {x1 > 0}. 2. Three successive phases of moving full-box fields, with initial label (0, 0, 0) and detector {x1 < −1}. In each case the particle enters the detector at some real time if and only if the machine halts. The repeated part of the prescription depends only on the machine; the input appears only in a one-time loading pulse.
